g.text: B. Stool studies reporting each core taxon ↓ or ↑

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 15px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #0b0b0b

g.text: The 17 taxa reported decreased in stool in all three conditions: 9 genera and 8 higher-rank nodes

text.style: font-size: 10.5px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #52514e

g.text: 7 of them had more decreased than increased stool studies in every condition. Keeping only genus and species ranks gives mean d_J = 0.478, close to the primary 0.479.

text.style: font-size: 7.5px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; fill: #8a8984

g.text: Dot: blue when ↓ studies outnumber ↑, red when ↑ outnumber ↓, grey when equal. Upper block:

text.style: font-size: 7.5px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; fill: #8a8984

g.text: genera; lower block: family, order, class and phylum nodes, whose annotations are rolled up

text.style: font-size: 7.5px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; fill: #8a8984

g.text: from descendant taxa. Net ↓ = more decreased than increased studies in every condition.

text.style: font-size: 7.5px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; fill: #8a8984

g.text: A taxon is in a condition's set when at least one decreased stool signature reports it; the counts in B show that some core taxa are also reported increased, sometimes more often (for example Oscillospiraceae

text.style: font-size: 7.5px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; fill: #8a8984

g.text: in PD and Bacteroidota in CRC). PD, Parkinson's disease; HIV, HIV infection; CRC, colorectal cancer. BugSigDB 2026-04-24_00:41_UTC; human profiles; condition and body site from each experiment's own record.
